prerequisites: Prior knowledge equivalent to a degree in basic energy efficiency analysis (Technical Thermodynamics, Heat Transfer, and Fluid Mechanics).

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context.

Students should know how to apply acquired knowledge and their problem-solving ability in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.

Students should be able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on information that, being incomplete or limited, includes reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students should know how to communicate their conclusions and the ultimate knowledge and reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Students should possess learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous manner.
The ability to solve problems in new or unfamiliar environments within multidisciplinary contexts related to energy engineering.
The ability to integrate knowledge to formulate applications for the development of new energy technologies.

The ability for autonomous learning that allows continued study through the development of the capacity to search for specialized documentation in cutting-edge scientific-technical literature and its assimilation.
Ability to identify, analyze, and evaluate the basic dominant phenomena in fluid-mechanical processes and energy transfer and utilization in engineering and industry.
Fundamental analysis of fluid-mechanical and thermal problems of interest in the energy industry, identifying strong and weak variables and evaluating possible simplifying hypotheses.
Ability to study, propose, and apply different types of technologies to improve the utilization and energy efficiency of installations or plants, comparing alternatives by performance and costs.
Ability for thermodynamic and economic analysis of installations and their elements, for the evaluation of energy efficiency.
Know and apply European Directives and current regulations in Spain aimed at energy saving and improving energy efficiency in industrial facilities.
Know the key aspects to evaluate and the phases to carry out in an industrial energy audit.
Identify and assess possible energy saving and efficiency measures in horizontal systems and productive processes applicable to the industrial sector.
Understand the fundamentals of cogeneration and its associated technologies, as well as applicable legislation.
Work on practical cases of energy auditing in the industrial sector, evaluating the improvements achieved with different technological solutions.

syllabus_topics: Energy auditing and management in industry.
Energy efficiency in horizontal systems and technologies (processes, equipment, and systems present in all types of industries: boilers, motors, combustion, insulation, etc.).
Energy efficiency in productive processes (textile, cement, ceramic, etc.) and cogeneration.
Practical cases of energy audits in different industrial sectors.
assessment_rules: For students with continuous assessment, if the written exam score is 3.5 or higher, the final grade is calculated as (0.2 * IP) + (0.3 * ECP) + (0.5 * EX). If the written exam score is below 3.5, the final grade is the exam score. To pass the course, the final grade must be 5.0 or higher. For extraordinary calls, a minimum of 3.5 out of 10 in the theoretical exam is required. If this minimum is met, the final grade is calculated using the continuous assessment formula, otherwise, the grade is the exam score.
